Properties CurrentTransaction Gets the current active transaction, or null if no transaction is active. public IDbContextTransaction? CurrentTransaction { get; } Property Value IDbContextTransaction Methods AcquireTransactionLockAsync(string, CancellationToken) Acquires an exclusive, database-wide lock identified by name, held until the current transaction commits or rolls back. Callers competing for the same name are serialized; different names never block each other. public Task AcquireTransactionLockAsync(string name, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters name string Lock name. Identifies what is being serialized, e.g. "contract-number:53". cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task A task that completes once the lock is held. Remarks Use it to serialize a read-then-write that the schema alone cannot make atomic — allocating the next value of a per-tenant sequence, for instance, where every writer reads the same maximum and collides on a unique index. It is an advisory lock: it guards nothing by itself, only callers that ask for the same name. A transaction must be active (see BeginTransactionAsync(CancellationToken)). Without one the lock is released as soon as the statement ends and protects nothing, so the call throws instead. The statement itself lives in the provider package — pg_advisory_xact_lock in NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL, sp_getapplock (LockOwner Transaction) in NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer — behind IDbContextTransactionLock, and is registered by that package's AddDatabase helpers. With no such package in play (an in-memory context built by hand in a test) there is nothing to serialize and the call does nothing. api/data/NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCo.title: Interface IDbContextTransactionLock | Nuv Tools Framework
api/data/NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCo.summary: Interface IDbContextTransactionLock Namespace NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.Context Assembly NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.dll Provider-specific implementation of the transaction-scoped lock behind AcquireTransactionLockAsync(string, CancellationToken). public interface IDbContextTransactionLock Remarks Every relational database offers this, under a different name and keyed differently — pg_advisory_xact_lock on PostgreSQL, sp_getapplock on SQL Server — so the statement lives in the provider package, not here. The implementation is registered by that package's AddDatabase/AddDatabaseByConnectionName helpers, and DbContextBase resolves it from the application service provider. Methods AcquireAsync(DbContext, string, CancellationToken) Acquires the exclusive lock named name, blocking until it is granted, and holds it until the current transaction of context ends. Task AcquireAsync(DbContext context, string name, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters context DbContext The context whose transaction and connection the lock belongs to. name string Lock name, as given by the caller. cancellationToken CancellationToken A cancellation token to observe while waiting for the task to complete. Returns Task A task that completes once the lock is held.

api/data/NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCo.summary: Class PostgreSqlTransactionLock Namespace NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.Context Assembly NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.dll PostgreSQL implementation of IDbContextTransactionLock, on top of pg_advisory_xact_lock: blocks until the lock is granted and releases it when the transaction ends. public sealed class PostgreSqlTransactionLock : IDbContextTransactionLock Inheritance object PostgreSqlTransactionLock Implements IDbContextTransactionLock Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks PostgreSQL keys advisory locks by a 64-bit integer, so the caller's name is hashed into one. api/data/NuvTools.Data.Paging.Enumeratio.title: Enum PagingCountMode | Nuv Tools Framework
api/data/NuvTools.Data.Paging.Enumeratio.summary: Enum PagingCountMode Namespace NuvTools.Data.Paging.Enumerations Assembly NuvTools.Data.dll Specifies how the total count is determined during paging operations. public enum PagingCountMode Fields Normal = 0 Performs a full COUNT(*) query to determine the total number of items. This is the default behavior and provides an exact total. SkipCount = 1 Skips the COUNT(*) query for better performance on large datasets. Instead, fetches one extra item to determine if a next page exists. The Total property will be set to -1 to indicate the count is unknown.

Methods SendAsync(MailMessage, CancellationToken) Sends an email message asynchronously using the configured SMTP server. public Task<MailSendResult> SendAsync(MailMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters request MailMessage The mail message to send, including sender, recipients, subject, body, and optional attachments. cancellationToken CancellationToken The token to monitor for cancellation requests. api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Contracts.I.title: Interface IPaymentRefundClient | Nuv Tools Framework
api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Contracts.I.summary: Interface IPaymentRefundClient Namespace NuvTools.Payment.Contracts Assembly NuvTools.Payment.dll Giving money back: refunding part or all of a payment the customer already made. public interface IPaymentRefundClient Remarks Separate from IPaymentChargeClient, for the reason charges and transfers are separate. Refunding is not the inverse of charging: it names a payment rather than a customer, it can be partial and repeated until the payment is exhausted, and a caller that can charge is not automatically a caller that may give money back. Keeping it its own contract lets a provider that cannot refund simply not implement it, and lets a composition root grant the two capabilities separately. What it does not do is claw back a payee. Money already transferred to a payee is the caller's problem to reconcile — by netting it off what the payee is owed next, which is a decision only the caller can make. A provider API that reverses a transfer exists, but using it would take money out of an account the payee may have already spent from. Methods RefundAsync(PaymentRefundRequest, CancellationToken) Refunds a payment, in whole or in part. api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Enumeration.title: Enum PaymentEventType | Nuv Tools Framework
api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Enumeration.summary: Enum PaymentEventType Namespace NuvTools.Payment.Enumerations Assembly NuvTools.Payment.dll The kinds of webhook a payment provider sends that a caller is expected to act on. public enum PaymentEventType Fields PayeeAccountUpdated = 1 What the provider allows a payee to do has changed — being paid out, most of all. PaymentFailed = 4 A payment was refused. PaymentMethodSaved = 2 A customer saved a payment method, and it can now be charged off-session. PaymentRefunded = 5 A payment was refunded, in whole or in part. Sent for a refund the caller asked for and for one raised at the provider — a dispute resolved in the customer's favour, or somebody acting in the provider's dashboard. That is why it is worth acting on rather than inferring from the caller's own refund call: the caller's records are otherwise the last to know. PaymentSucceeded = 3 A payment settled. Unknown = 0 Not one of the events below. Record it and ignore it. Remarks A provider client maps its own event names onto these. Anything it does not recognise arrives as Unknown rather than being dropped, because a caller still has to record that a delivery happened — an endpoint that fails on an event it has no use for makes the provider retry it for days.

api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Enumeration.title: Enum PaymentStatusType | Nuv Tools Framework
api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Enumeration.summary: Enum PaymentStatusType Namespace NuvTools.Payment.Enumerations Assembly NuvTools.Payment.dll What became of one payment, in the few outcomes a caller can act on. public enum PaymentStatusType Fields Failed = 4 Refused, and nothing was taken. Retrying needs a new attempt. Pending = 1 Taken, not settled: the provider has it and has not said yes or no yet. RequiresAction = 3 The customer has to finish it — a card asking for its owner to be present, typically. Not a refusal: charging again would be charging twice. Succeeded = 2 The money arrived. The only outcome that clears a debt. Remarks Providers report far more states than this, and they all name them differently. These four are the ones that change what the caller does next, so a provider client maps its own vocabulary onto them and keeps the rest to itself.

Listed whole and cached for NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieContractProvider.CacheDuration, never consulted one by one. A screen that shows contracts in a grid would otherwise ask Omie once per row, and Omie answers a burst of repeated calls with "Consumo redundante detectado" — which blocks the app_key for every other integration, not just the grid. OmieDirectApiClient Raw call to the Omie API, for the registrations IOmieApiClient does not cover or covers without the fields a caller needs. It concentrates three details that any new call would otherwise repeat: the Content-Type goes without the charset parameter — with it, the Omie gateway answers a SOAP "Bad Request" envelope (and that is exactly what PostAsJsonAsync/JsonContent would send); business errors come in the body (faultstring) alongside an HTTP 5xx — without reading it, the failure turns into an "InternalServerError" that says nothing; consumption refusals (REDUNDANT, MISUSE_API_PROCESS) are not request errors and get their own treatment (see IsThrottled(string?)). OmieServiceCatalogProvider Omie service catalog, read whole (ListarCadastroServico, paginated) and indexed by the business code (cCodigo) — the code applications store in their own configuration. This is how the nCodServico, the description and the unit price of a service are discovered: Omie exposes no search by cCodigo, so the catalog is listed and searched in memory. The result is cached for NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient.Services.OmieServiceCatalogProvider.CacheDuration because Omie refuses repeated ListarCadastroServico calls in a short window ("Consumo redundante detectado") — without the cache, opening a screen and generating a service order right after would drop the second call. OmieServiceOrderBillingProvider Invoicing of a single service order in Omie — the documented path to issue the NFS-e of one OS, which IOmieApiClient does not cover and therefore goes through the direct client: StatusOS (servicos/os/): fiscal state of the order — stage, whether it was cancelled, whether it was already invoiced and the NFS-e that came out of it. It is the query that says whether there is anything to do, and the one that confirms the result afterwards. ValidarOS (servicos/osp/): Omie's validation before invoicing. It is what points out, in the API's own words, which required data is missing on the order or on the client registration — instead of finding out through the city hall's rejection, after the invoice was already requested. FaturarOS (servicos/osp/): invoices that order. The equivalent of "Faturar Selecionada" in the Omie UI — not to be confused with FaturarLoteOS (servicos/oslote/), which invoices every order of a stage and, triggered for one client, would take the others along. None of them invents data: the invoice content is the order's. What is decided here is only when to ask for the invoice.

api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiCli.summary: Namespace NuvTools.Payment.Omie.ApiClient Classes DependencyInjection Extensions to register the Omie API client in the DI container. OmieFaultClassifier Classifies Omie failure messages so callers can react programmatically (e.g. switch an OS create to an update when the integration code already exists) instead of string-matching Omie text themselves. This component surfaces faults as failed IResult (it deliberately does not throw — see the comment on OmieApiClient._staticClient), so the markers live here in one place. VERIFY (Omie test app): confirm the exact faultstring wording for the duplicate-integration-code and not-found cases against the current Omie responses and adjust the markers below if needed. OmieOrderStage The service order stage (cEtapa) in Omie. The API documents five values — 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 (invoice) — but an account may have its own Kanban columns, and the query returns the real stage (60 has been seen). Echoing that stage back on a change means sending a value outside the domain the API accepts; since cEtapa is optional on AlterarOS, the right move is to omit it and leave the order where it is. OmiePaymentTerm The payment term code (cCodParc) of a service order in Omie. It is not a preference: it tells Omie whether the installments come from a registered payment condition or from the request itself.

api/payment/NuvTools.Payment.Stripe.ApiC.summary: Class StripeRefundApiClient Namespace NuvTools.Payment.Stripe.ApiClient.Services Assembly NuvTools.Payment.Stripe.ApiClient.dll Giving money back: refunding part or all of a payment the customer already made. public class StripeRefundApiClient : IPaymentRefundClient Inheritance object StripeRefundApiClient Implements IPaymentRefundClient Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Separate from IPaymentChargeClient, for the reason charges and transfers are separate. Refunding is not the inverse of charging: it names a payment rather than a customer, it can be partial and repeated until the payment is exhausted, and a caller that can charge is not automatically a caller that may give money back. Keeping it its own contract lets a provider that cannot refund simply not implement it, and lets a composition root grant the two capabilities separately. What it does not do is claw back a payee. Money already transferred to a payee is the caller's problem to reconcile — by netting it off what the payee is owed next, which is a decision only the caller can make. A provider API that reverses a transfer exists, but using it would take money out of an account the payee may have already spent from. Returns RateLimiterOptions The options for chaining. Remarks The partition key is the policy name followed by the address. Each policy therefore counts on its own: using up the allowance for asking for a reset link does not use up the allowance for spending one. There is no queue. A caller past the limit gets the rejection straight away instead of having its connection held open. The address is RemoteIpAddress. Behind a proxy, call UseForwardedHeaders before UseRateLimiter, or every caller shares the proxy's address. A request with no address falls into one shared bucket rather than going unlimited. An address is something a caller can vary, so this bounds noise and unsophisticated scripts; it does not replace account lockout or a uniform answer that hides whether an account exists. SetTooManyRequests(OnRejectedContext) Sets the response status to 429 and, when the limiter knows it, the Retry-After header in seconds. public static void SetTooManyRequests(this OnRejectedContext context) Parameters context OnRejectedContext The context passed to OnRejected. Remarks Writes no body, so an API can add its own error envelope and a page can render its own message.

The client signs the challenge in the browser with Web PKI (signWithRestPki); the service validates possession of the private key and the trust chain, and the subject is read from the certificate it validated. RestPkiDocumentSigner Signs PDFs (PAdES) through Lacuna REST PKI. The client signs the challenge in the browser with Web PKI (signWithRestPki); reading certificates, preparing the document and completing the signature all happen on the service, so no key or licence is kept locally. RestPkiOptions Configuration for certificate authentication through Lacuna REST PKI.

api/security/NuvTools.Security.Certifica.title: Interface IDocumentSigner | Nuv Tools Framework
api/security/NuvTools.Security.Certifica.summary: Interface IDocumentSigner Namespace NuvTools.Security.Certificate.Signing Assembly NuvTools.Security.dll Signs a PDF with a digital certificate whose private key stays with the person, in two steps: the server prepares the document and opens a challenge, the client signs it, and the server completes the signature. public interface IDocumentSigner Remarks Whatever the application needs to know about who signed — to check it is the expected person, or to print it on the document — comes from the certificate the provider read, never from a value the client sends. Provider failures propagate as exceptions. Signing is not an access decision, so there is no safe outcome to fall back to: the caller reports that the document was not signed. Methods CompleteAsync(string, CancellationToken) Completes the signature the client signed the challenge for. Task<SignedDocument> CompleteAsync(string token, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters token string The token of the challenge the client signed. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<SignedDocument> The signed PDF and the certificate it was actually signed with. GetSignersAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) Reads the certificates a document was already signed with, without validating the signatures. Task<IReadOnlyList<CertificateDetails>> GetSignersAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> signedDocument, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters signedDocument ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The signed PDF. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<IReadOnlyList<CertificateDetails>> One entry per signature, in the order the provider reports them. Document timestamps are left out. ReadCertificateAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CancellationToken) Reads who a certificate was issued to, without validating it. Task<CertificateDetails> ReadCertificateAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> certificate, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters certificate ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The certificate, DER-encoded. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<CertificateDetails> What the certificate says about its holder and issuer. StartAsync(DocumentSignatureRequest, CancellationToken) Prepares the document for signing and opens the challenge the client signs. Task<DocumentSignatureChallenge> StartAsync(DocumentSignatureRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters request DocumentSignatureRequest The PDF and, optionally, the visible stamp of this signature. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<DocumentSignatureChallenge> The challenge the client signs and sends back.

api/security/NuvTools.Security.Extension.summary: Class ClaimExtensions Namespace NuvTools.Security.Extensions Assembly NuvTools.Security.dll Provides extension methods for working with collections of Claim objects. public static class ClaimExtensions Inheritance object ClaimExtensions Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks These extensions simplify the process of adding permission claims and bulk-adding claims from static class constants. Methods AddByClass(List<Claim>, string, Type) Adds claims to the collection by reading all public static string constants from a specified class type. public static void AddByClass(this List<Claim> claims, string claimType, Type classType) Parameters claims List<Claim> The list of claims to add to. claimType string The claim type to assign to all extracted values. classType Type The type of the class containing the constant values. Examples public static class UserPermissions { public const string Read = "users.read"; public const string Write = "users.write"; public const string Delete = "users.delete"; } var claims = new List<Claim>(); claims.AddByClass("permission", typeof(UserPermissions)); // Results in 3 claims with type "permission" and values "users.read", "users.write", "users.delete" Remarks This method uses reflection to find all public, static, readonly string fields in the specified class and creates a claim for each one using the specified claim type. This is useful when you have a permissions class with multiple permission constant values. AddPermission(List<Claim>, string) Adds a permission claim to the claims collection. public static void AddPermission(this List<Claim> claims, string value) Parameters claims List<Claim> The list of claims to add to. value string The permission value to add. Examples var claims = new List<Claim>(); claims.AddPermission("users.read"); claims.AddPermission("users.write"); Remarks This is a convenience method that creates a claim with the Permission claim type. AddPermissionByClass(List<Claim>, Type) Adds permission claims to the collection by reading all public static string constants from a specified class type. public static void AddPermissionByClass(this List<Claim> claims, Type classType) Parameters claims List<Claim> The list of claims to add to. classType Type The type of the class containing the permission constant values. Examples public static class UserPermissions { public const string Read = "users.read"; public const string Write = "users.write"; } var claims = new List<Claim>(); claims.AddPermissionByClass(typeof(UserPermissions)); // Results in 2 permission claims Remarks This is a convenience method that calls AddByClass(List<Claim>, string, Type) with Permission as the claim type.

Methods GetCustomAttributeValues<T>(ClaimsPrincipal, string) Gets all values from a custom extension attribute claim and parses them as the specified type. public static IEnumerable<T>? GetCustomAttributeValues<T>(this ClaimsPrincipal user, string customAttributeName) Parameters user ClaimsPrincipal The claims principal representing the user. customAttributeName string The name of the custom attribute (without the "extension_" prefix). Returns IEnumerable<T> A collection of parsed values, or null if the claim doesn't exist. Invalid values are filtered out for enum types. Type Parameters T The type to parse the attribute values as (string, int, double, bool, or enum). Examples // Get a list of role IDs stored as integers in an extension attribute var roleIds = user.GetCustomAttributeValues<int>("roleIds"); // Get an enum value from a custom attribute var permissions = user.GetCustomAttributeValues<PermissionLevel>("permissions"); Remarks This method looks for a claim with type "extension_{customAttributeName}" and expects a comma-separated list of values. It parses each value to the specified type. Supported types: string, int, double, bool, and enum types. This is commonly used with Azure AD B2C custom attributes that are passed as extension claims. Exceptions NotSupportedException Thrown when the type T is not supported. FormatException Thrown when values cannot be parsed to the specified type. GetEmail(ClaimsPrincipal) Gets the email address of the user, checking multiple claim sources and validating the format. public static string? Remarks This method checks the following claims in order: Email, email (OIDC), UPN, PreferredUsername, UniqueName. GetSub(this ClaimsPrincipal user) Parameters user ClaimsPrincipal The claims principal representing the user. Returns string The subject identifier, or null if not present. Remarks The 'sub' claim is the standard JWT claim for the unique user identifier. GetSurname(ClaimsPrincipal) Gets the surname (last name) of the user from the Surname claim. public static string? Remarks UPN is commonly used in Microsoft Azure AD and Active Directory scenarios. It typically has the format username@domain. HasValue<T>(ClaimsPrincipal, string, T) Determines whether the user has a specific value in a custom extension attribute claim. public static bool HasValue<T>(this ClaimsPrincipal user, string customAttriuteName, T value) Parameters user ClaimsPrincipal The claims principal representing the user. customAttriuteName string The name of the custom attribute (without the "extension_" prefix). value T The value to check for. api/security/NuvTools.Security.Network.N.title: Class NetworkAddressPolicy | Nuv Tools Framework
api/security/NuvTools.Security.Network.N.summary: Class NetworkAddressPolicy Namespace NuvTools.Security.Network Assembly NuvTools.Security.dll Decides whether an outbound connection may reach an address: the building block against server-side request forgery (SSRF) when an application fetches a URL somebody else supplied. public sealed class NetworkAddressPolicy Inheritance object NetworkAddressPolicy Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The decision is taken on the IP address, never on the text of the URL. A host name proves nothing about where it resolves — a public domain can carry an A record of 10.0.0.5, and can change it between a check and the connection (DNS rebinding). Pair this policy with PublicNetworkConnector, which applies it to the address a socket actually connects to. By default only publicly routable unicast addresses are allowed. Denied: loopback, private (RFC 1918 and IPv6 unique-local), link-local (which includes the cloud instance metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254), carrier-grade NAT, documentation and benchmarking ranges, multicast, reserved space, the IPv6 transition prefixes that embed an IPv4 address, and Azure's platform address 168.63.129.16, which is public in form and internal in fact. Constructors NetworkAddressPolicy(IEnumerable<IPNetwork>?, IEnumerable<IPNetwork>?, IEnumerable<string>?) Creates a policy. public NetworkAddressPolicy(IEnumerable<IPNetwork>? allowedNetworks = null, IEnumerable<IPNetwork>? additionalDeniedNetworks = null, IEnumerable<string>? additionalDeniedHostSuffixes = null) Parameters allowedNetworks IEnumerable<IPNetwork> Networks allowed even though the defaults deny them — an internal backend a deployment trusts. Checked before the denied list, so keep it as narrow as the need. additionalDeniedNetworks IEnumerable<IPNetwork> Networks denied on top of the defaults. additionalDeniedHostSuffixes IEnumerable<string> Host name suffixes denied on top of the defaults. Properties PublicOnly A policy allowing publicly routable addresses only. public static NetworkAddressPolicy PublicOnly { get; } Property Value NetworkAddressPolicy Methods IsAllowed(IPAddress) Whether a connection to this address is allowed. public bool IsAllowed(IPAddress address) Parameters address IPAddress Returns bool Remarks An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:127.0.0.1) is judged as the IPv4 address it carries, which is where the socket ends up. IsHostAllowed(string) Whether a host name may be looked up at all. Names that can only mean "inside" — localhost and the internal suffixes — are refused without asking DNS. public bool IsHostAllowed(string host) Parameters host string Returns bool ResolveAllowedAsync(string, CancellationToken) Resolves a host and returns its addresses, throwing when the name or any address it resolves to is not allowed. public Task<IPAddress[]> ResolveAllowedAsync(string host, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters host string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<IPAddress[]> Remarks Any denied address refuses the whole name, not just that address. A name answering with one public and one private address is either misconfigured or an attempt to win a race, and neither is worth connecting to. Exceptions NetworkAddressNotAllowedException The host or one of its addresses is denied.

api/security/NuvTools.Security.Network.P.title: Class PublicNetworkConnector | Nuv Tools Framework
api/security/NuvTools.Security.Network.P.summary: Class PublicNetworkConnector Namespace NuvTools.Security.Network Assembly NuvTools.Security.dll Makes a SocketsHttpHandler connect only to addresses a NetworkAddressPolicy allows, judged at the moment of connecting. public static class PublicNetworkConnector Inheritance object PublicNetworkConnector Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Why at the socket and not before the request. Checking a URL, resolving it and then letting HttpClient resolve it again leaves a gap an attacker controls: their DNS answers a public address to the check and a private one to the connection. Here the address that is checked is the address the socket connects to — there is no second lookup. Every connection goes through the callback, redirects included, so a public URL answering 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/ is refused at the second hop. The proxy is switched off, because through a proxy the callback would only ever see the proxy's address. Works with anything built on SocketsHttpHandler: an HttpClient, an IHttpClientFactory primary handler, or a reverse proxy's forwarder handler. Methods Apply(SocketsHttpHandler, NetworkAddressPolicy?) Applies the policy to an existing handler, replacing its connect callback and its proxy. public static void Apply(SocketsHttpHandler handler, NetworkAddressPolicy? policy = null) Parameters handler SocketsHttpHandler The handler to restrict. policy NetworkAddressPolicy The policy; PublicOnly when omitted. CreateConnectCallback(NetworkAddressPolicy) The connect callback itself, for a handler configured elsewhere. public static Func<SocketsHttpConnectionContext, CancellationToken, ValueTask<Stream>> CreateConnectCallback(NetworkAddressPolicy policy) Parameters policy NetworkAddressPolicy Returns Func<SocketsHttpConnectionContext, CancellationToken, ValueTask<Stream>> CreateHandler(NetworkAddressPolicy?) Creates a handler that connects only where policy allows. public static SocketsHttpHandler CreateHandler(NetworkAddressPolicy? policy = null) Parameters policy NetworkAddressPolicy The policy; PublicOnly when omitted. Returns SocketsHttpHandler

api/security/NuvTools.Security.Signing.A.summary: Class KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider Namespace NuvTools.Security.Signing.Azure Assembly NuvTools.Security.Signing.Azure.dll Signs with an RSA key kept in Azure Key Vault. The private key never leaves the vault: this process holds the public half of each version and asks the vault for every signature. public class KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider : ISigningKeyProvider, IDisposable Inheritance object KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider Implements ISigningKeyProvider IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Every enabled version of the key that is within its validity period is offered, so tokens signed before a rotation keep validating. A new version starts signing once it has been published for ActivationDelay. The list of versions is read again every RefreshInterval. When the vault cannot be reached for that, the last list read keeps being served: a rotation noticed late is better than no token at all. The identity used needs to list and read the key and to sign with it — the Key Vault Crypto User role covers both. Constructors KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider(KeyClient, TokenCredential, IOptions<KeyVaultSigningOptions>, TimeProvider, ILogger<KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider>) Creates the provider. public KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider(KeyClient keys, TokenCredential credential, IOptions<KeyVaultSigningOptions> options, TimeProvider time, ILogger<KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider> logger) Parameters keys KeyClient The client for the vault holding the key. credential TokenCredential The identity the signatures are requested with. options IOptions<KeyVaultSigningOptions> Which key to use and how its rotation is followed. time TimeProvider The clock the activation delay and the refresh are measured on. logger ILogger<KeyVaultSigningKeyProvider> Where a failed refresh is reported. articles/architecture.html.title: Architecture | Nuv Tools Framework
articles/architecture.html.summary:
Architecture The framework is organized in eight areas. Packages in one area may build on the foundation and on other areas, never the other way round, so referencing a package never drags in an unrelated stack. Areas and how they depend on each other flowchart BT subgraph Foundation Common["Common"] Resources["Resources"] Validation["Validation"] end Data["Data
+ EF Core, SQL Server, PostgreSQL"] Web["ASP.NET Core and Blazor"] Security["Security and identity"] Notification["Notifications"] Report["Reports"] Storage["Storage and ledger"] Payment["Payments"] Data --> Common Web --> Data Web --> Common Security --> Common Security --> Resources Security --> Validation Security --> Data Security --> Web Payment --> Common classDef standalone fill:#fff3ea,stroke:#e96b20,color:#04425b class Notification,Report,Storage standalone Notifications, reports and storage (in orange) depend on no other Nuv Tools package: they can be used in any .NET application on their own. Contracts and providers Every area that talks to an outside service splits in two kinds of package: The contract — interfaces and models, no vendor SDK. Application code references only this. One package per provider — the implementation and its Add… registration. Only the host project references it. flowchart TB subgraph Contracts Mail["Notification.Mail"] Messaging["Notification.Messaging"] Realtime["Notification.Realtime"] Storage["Storage"] Ledger["Blockchain"] Payment["Payment"] Sec["Security
signing, certificate, biometrics"] end subgraph Providers Smtp["Mail.Smtp"] --> Mail Twilio["Mail.Twilio"] --> Mail SB["Messaging.Azure.ServiceBus"] --> Messaging SR["Realtime.Azure.SignalR"] --> Realtime Blob["Storage.Azure"] --> Storage ACL["Blockchain.Azure"] --> Ledger Stripe["Payment.Stripe.ApiClient"] --> Payment KV["Security.Signing.Azure"] --> Sec Lacuna["Security.Certificate.Lacuna"] --> Sec Serpro["Security.Biometrics.Serpro"] --> Sec end classDef provider fill:#fff3ea,stroke:#e96b20,color:#04425b class Smtp,Twilio,SB,SR,Blob,ACL,Stripe,KV,Lacuna,Serpro provider The vendor SDK (MailKit, Azure SDKs, Stripe.net, Lacuna REST PKI) is referenced only by its provider package, so a contract never pulls a vendor into your domain or application layer. Inside a request A typical ASP.NET Core API built on the framework, from the request to the database and back: sequenceDiagram autonumber participant Client participant API as ASP.NET Core endpoint participant Auth as Security.Identity + Security.AspNetCore participant Service as Service (AspNetCore.EntityFrameworkCore) participant Db as DbContextBase (Data.EntityFrameworkCore) Client->>API: HTTP request + JWT API->>Auth: check permission policies Auth-->>API: current user API->>Service: call with a form or filter Service->>Db: query with paging, sorting, filters Db-->>Service: IResult with data Service-->>API: IResult API-->>Client: response with data and messages Where each package lives Each area is a separate repository under github.com/nuvtools, released with its own pipeline. The guides link to each repository, and the API reference is generated from the same sources.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | Nuv Tools Framework
articles/getting-started.html.summary:
Getting started The framework is a set of independent NuGet packages. Reference only the ones you need; each brings the Nuv Tools packages it builds on. Requirements .NET 8, 9 or 10. Every package targets all three. Packages that talk to a cloud service (Azure, Twilio, Stripe, Lacuna, SERPRO) need that service's account and credentials; the rest have no external requirement. Install dotnet add package NuvTools.Common Add the contract your application code uses, and the provider package only where you compose the application: # Application layer: the contract dotnet add package NuvTools.Notification.Mail # Host project: the provider dotnet add package NuvTools.Notification.Mail.Smtp Register and use Providers register themselves on IServiceCollection and bind their settings from configuration. { "MailSmtp": { "Host": "smtp.example.com", "Port": 587, "UserName": "app@example.com" } } Keep MailSmtp:Password out of the file: set it with user secrets locally and a key vault or an environment variable when deployed. // Program.cs — the only place that knows the provider builder.Services.AddSmtpMail(builder.Configuration); // Anywhere else — only the contract public class WelcomeMail(IMailService mail) { public Task SendAsync(string to, CancellationToken cancellationToken) => mail.SendAsync(new MailMessage { From = new MailAddress { Address = "no-reply@example.com", DisplayName = "Example" }, To = [new MailAddress { Address = to }], Subject = "Welcome", Body = "

Your account is ready.

" }, cancellationToken); } Each provider's guide lists its settings section and options; for e-mail, see Mail. Report outcomes with results Services across the framework answer with IResult / IResult from NuvTools.Common, so success, validation failures and errors travel the same way from the data layer to the API. using NuvTools.Common.ResultWrapper; public IResult GetUser(int id) { if (id <= 0) return Result.ValidationFail("Invalid user ID"); var user = repository.FindById(id); if (user is null) return Result.FailNotFound("User not found"); return Result.Success(user); } flowchart LR Call["Operation"] --> Q{Outcome} Q -->|Success| S["Result.Success
Data + messages"] Q -->|Invalid input| V["Result.ValidationFail
field messages"] Q -->|Missing| N["Result.FailNotFound"] Q -->|Error| F["Result.Fail
logged with ILogger"] classDef ok fill:#e6f4fa,stroke:#0090c6,color:#04425b classDef bad fill:#fff3ea,stroke:#e96b20,color:#04425b class S ok class V,N,F bad The NuvTools.Common guide covers the full result API, including HTTP conversion with ToResultAsync(). Versions The major version follows .NET: 10.x packages are built for the .NET 10 generation (and still target 8 and 9). A minor version marks a breaking change; everything else is a patch. Next steps Browse the guides by area. Look up any type in the API reference. See how the areas relate in Architecture.

guides/data/data/README.html.title: Nuv Tools Data Libraries | Nuv Tools Framework
guides/data/data/README.html.summary: Nuv Tools Data Libraries Nuv Tools Data Libraries are a set of .NET libraries designed to simplify and standardize data access and manipulation. They provide abstractions and helpers for common data operations, as well as seamless integration with Entity Framework Core for SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Key Features Multi-Framework Support: .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10 ORM-Agnostic Core: Base paging and sorting utilities work with any data source EF Core Integration: First-class support for Entity Framework Core 10.0 Result Pattern: All database operations return IResult or IResult<T> for consistent error handling Async-First: All EF Core operations are async with CancellationToken support Bulk Operations: Efficient bulk add, update, and remove operations Well-Documented: Comprehensive XML documentation for IntelliSense support Libraries Overview NuvTools.Data Core library with generic helpers for data manipulation: Paging: Abstracts paging logic for both IQueryable and IEnumerable collections Sorting: Extension methods for sorting with ascending/descending direction Filtering: Paging filters with optional sorting capabilities No dependencies: Works with any data source or ORM dotnet add package NuvTools.Data NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore Extensions for Entity Framework Core: DbContextBase: Base class with CRUD operations using Result pattern Transaction Management: Built-in transaction support with rollback/commit Transaction Locks: AcquireTransactionLockAsync(name) serializes competing writers across processes (pg_advisory_xact_lock on PostgreSQL, sp_getapplock on SQL Server), released with the transaction Execution Strategies: Connection resiliency with automatic retry Bulk Operations: SyncFromListAsync, AddOrUpdateFromListAsync, AddOrRemoveFromListAsync Async Paging: PagingWrapAsync for efficient database paging dotnet add package NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer Specialized helpers for SQL Server with EF Core: Simple Registration: AddDatabase and AddDatabaseByConnectionName extension methods Configuration Integration: Load connection strings from appsettings.json SQL Server Options: Configure SQL Server-specific options via SqlServerDbContextOptionsBuilder dotnet add package NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL Specialized helpers for PostgreSQL with EF Core: Simple Registration: AddDatabase and AddDatabaseByConnectionName extension methods Snake Case Convention: UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention for PostgreSQL naming standards Npgsql Options: Configure PostgreSQL-specific options via NpgsqlDbContextOptionsBuilder dotnet add package NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL Quick Start Basic Paging (NuvTools.Data) using NuvTools.Data.Paging; // In-memory paging (0-indexed) var items = new List<Product> { /* ... */ }; var pagedResult = items.PagingWrap(pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 20); Console.WriteLine($"Page {pagedResult.PageIndex + 1} of {Math.Ceiling(pagedResult.Total / 20.0)}"); foreach (var item in pagedResult.List) { Console.WriteLine(item.Name); } Sorting (NuvTools.Data) using NuvTools.Data.Sorting; using NuvTools.Data.Sorting.Enumerations; var sortedProducts = products .Sort(p => p.Category, SortDirection.ASC) .ThenSort(p => p.Price, SortDirection.DESC); SQL Server Registration (NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer) using NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer.Extensions; // In Program.cs or Startup.cs builder.Services.AddDatabaseByConnectionName<MyDbContext>("DefaultConnection"); // Or with connection string directly builder.Services.AddDatabase<MyDbContext>(connectionString); // With SQL Server-specific options builder.Services.AddDatabaseByConnectionName<MyDbContext>( "DefaultConnection", sqlServerOptions => sqlServerOptions.EnableRetryOnFailure() ); PostgreSQL with Snake Case (NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL) using NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.Extensions; // Register DbContext builder.Services.AddDatabaseByConnectionName<MyDbContext>("PostgresConnection"); // In your DbContext public class MyDbContext : DbContextBase { protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) { // Apply snake_case naming convention for PostgreSQL modelBuilder.UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention(); base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder); } } Using DbContextBase using NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.Context; public class MyDbContext : DbContextBase { public MyDbContext(DbContextOptions<MyDbContext> options) : base(options) { } public DbSet<Product> Products { get; set; } } // In your service public class ProductService { private readonly MyDbContext _context; public async Task<IResult<int>> CreateProductAsync(Product product) { // AddAndSaveAsync returns IResult<TKey> return await _context.AddAndSaveAsync<Product, int>(product); } public async Task<IResult> UpdateProductAsync(Product product, int id) { // UpdateAndSaveAsync returns IResult return await _context.UpdateAndSaveAsync(product, id); } public async Task<IResult> DeleteProductAsync(int id) { // RemoveAndSaveAsync returns IResult return await _context.RemoveAndSaveAsync<Product>(id); } } Serializing a read-then-write (DbContextBase) Allocating the next value of a per-tenant sequence is a read followed by a write, so every concurrent writer reads the same maximum and they collide on the unique index. An exclusive lock, held until the transaction ends, makes the pair atomic without changing the schema: using var transaction = await context.BeginTransactionAsync(cancellationToken); // Blocks only writers asking for this same name; other tenants keep running in parallel. await context.AcquireTransactionLockAsync($"invoice-number:{tenantId}", cancellationToken); invoice.Number = await context.Invoice .Where(i => i.TenantId == tenantId) .Select(i => i.Number) .DefaultIfEmpty() .MaxAsync(cancellationToken) + 1; context.Invoice.Add(invoice); await context.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken); await transaction.CommitAsync(cancellationToken); // releases the lock A abstração (IDbContextTransactionLock) fica em NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore e cada pacote de provider traz a sua implementação — pg_advisory_xact_lock em ...PostgreSQL, sp_getapplock em ...SqlServer —, registrada automaticamente pelos helpers AddDatabase/AddDatabaseByConnectionName. Sem nenhum provider registrado (contexto em memória montado à mão, nos testes) a chamada é inócua. Async Paging with EF Core using NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.Paging; public async Task<PagingWithEnumerableList<Product>> GetProductsAsync(int pageIndex, int pageSize) { var query = _context.Products.Where(p => p.IsActive); // PagingWrapAsync materializes the data (0-indexed) var pagedResult = await query.PagingWrapWithEnumerableListAsync(pageIndex, pageSize); return pagedResult; } SkipCount Mode for Large Datasets For large datasets where COUNT(*) is too slow, use PagingCountMode.SkipCount to skip the count query. Instead of counting all rows, it fetches one extra item to determine if a next page exists: using NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.Paging; using NuvTools.Data.Paging.Enumerations; public async Task<PagingWithEnumerableList<Product>> GetProductsAsync(int pageIndex, int pageSize) { var query = _context.Products.Where(p => p.IsActive).OrderBy(p => p.Id); // SkipCount: no COUNT(*) query, uses N+1 trick to detect next page var pagedResult = await query.PagingWrapWithEnumerableListAsync( pageIndex, pageSize, PagingCountMode.SkipCount); // pagedResult.HasNextPage => true if more items exist // pagedResult.Total => -1 (unknown) return pagedResult; } The PagingFilter class also supports CountMode, making it easy to pass from the UI: var filter = new PagingFilter<ProductSortColumn> { PageIndex = 0, PageSize = 25, SortColumn = ProductSortColumn.Name, CountMode = PagingCountMode.SkipCount // Skip expensive COUNT(*) }; Bulk Operations // Sync from list: Add new, update existing, remove missing var result = await _context.SyncFromListAsync( updatedProducts, p => p.Id, p => p.IsActive // Optional filter ); // Add or update only (no removal) await _context.AddOrUpdateFromListAsync(products, p => p.Id); // Add or remove only (no updates) await _context.AddOrRemoveFromListAsync(products, p => p.Id); 📋 Requirements .NET SDK: 8.0, 9.0, or 10.0 Entity Framework Core: 10.1.0 (for EF Core libraries) Database Providers: SQL Server: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer 10.1.0 PostgreSQL: Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL 10.0.0 🔧 Development Building the Solution dotnet build NuvTools.Data.slnx Running Tests # Run all tests dotnet test # Run specific test project dotnet test tests/NuvTools.Data.Test/NuvTools.Data.Test.csproj Creating NuGet Packages dotnet build NuvTools.Data.slnx -c Release Packages are automatically generated in bin/Release folders when building in Release configuration. 📝 Version History Version 10.1.4 New Feature: PagingCountMode.SkipCount to skip expensive COUNT(*) queries on large datasets New Feature: HasNextPage property on all paging results for infinite scroll / forward-only navigation New: PagingCountMode enum (Normal, SkipCount) in NuvTools.Data.Paging.Enumerations New: CountMode property on PagingFilter (defaults to Normal) New: PagingHelper.CalculateHasNextPage() helper method Breaking Change: PagingHelper.GetSkip() changed from internal to public Breaking Change: PagingWrapAsync and PagingWrapWithEnumerableListAsync have a new countMode parameter before cancellationToken. Callers passing CancellationToken positionally must switch to named parameter: cancellationToken: token Version 10.1.0 Breaking Change: Paging system migrated from 1-based PageNumber to 0-based PageIndex Property PageNumber renamed to PageIndex in PagingBase, PagingFilter, and paging results Method GetPageNumber() renamed to GetPageIndex() in PagingHelper Default page parameter changed from 1 to 0 Version 10.0.2 Updated to Entity Framework Core 10.0.2 Updated all Microsoft packages to version 10.0.2 Improved package descriptions and tags Copyright updated to 2026 Version 10.0.0 Added .NET 10 support Updated to Entity Framework Core 10.0.0 Updated all Microsoft packages to version 10.0.0 Comprehensive XML documentation added to all public APIs Migrated solution to .slnx format Releasing Publishing to nuget.org is irreversible per version, so the workflow makes it the last and smallest step. One workflow per library. Each package has its own, so a run and an approval each concern exactly one package. The steps themselves are shared, in the reusable package-publish.yml. Package Workflow Release tag NuvTools.Data data-publish.yml data-vX.Y.Z NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore entityframeworkcore-publish.yml entityframeworkcore-vX.Y.Z NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL postgresql-publish.yml postgresql-vX.Y.Z NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer sqlserver-publish.yml sqlserver-vX.Y.Z Set the package's <Version> in its .csproj and merge it. That is the version that gets published; the workflow reads it and never computes one. Run the library's workflow by hand (Actions → Data Publish → Run workflow) with push checked. The workflow builds the solution with -warnaserror, runs the tests, takes that package only from the build output, verifies it carries its README, licence, icon, symbols and every target framework, and then waits for approval on the nuget GitHub Environment before pushing. After the push succeeds, the workflow tags the commit with the tag in the table above. The tag is a record of what is on nuget.org, never what starts a release, so it cannot exist for a version that did not get there. A run whose tag already exists stops before building: the version has been released and <Version> needs a bump. A referenced package goes first. A package that references another of this repository as a project depends on whatever <Version> that one has in the commit. The workflow checks that version is on nuget.org and refuses to push a package whose dependency is not there yet. So: NuvTools.Data before NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore. NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore before NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL and NuvTools.Data.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer. That check knows a version exists, not what is in it: when a referenced package changes its public API, bump and publish it first, then bump and publish the packages built on it. Versions published by hand are refused. Releases made before these workflows exist on nuget.org with no tag. Pushing one again would skip the duplicate and then tag the current commit as a release it is not, so a version that is already on nuget.org stops the run. The exception is a re-run of the same run, which is how a push that succeeded and a tag that failed gets finished. No API key is stored. The push uses nuget.org's trusted publishing: the job presents a GitHub OIDC token, nuget.org checks it against the policy registered for this repository and answers with a key that lives for one hour. The repository needs one secret, NUGET_USER — the nuget.org profile name the policy belongs to — and the policy itself, registered under Trusted Publishing on nuget.org with the owner nuvtools, the repository nuvtools-data, the workflow file and the environment nuget. guides/foundation/common/README.html.title: NuvTools.Common | Nuv Tools Framework
guides/foundation/common/README.html.summary: NuvTools.Common A cross-platform utility library for .NET 8, 9, and 10, designed to streamline development for Web, Desktop, and Mobile (MAUI) applications. Installation Install via NuGet Package Manager: dotnet add package NuvTools.Common Or via Package Manager Console: Install-Package NuvTools.Common Overview NuvTools.Common provides a rich set of reusable components, extension methods, and helpers that address frequent programming needs, focusing on consistency, safety, and productivity. The library follows modern .NET best practices with nullable reference types, async/await patterns, and minimal dependencies. Key Features 1. ResultWrapper - Railway-Oriented Programming Standardize operation outcomes with a fluent result pattern supporting success, error, and validation states. using NuvTools.Common.ResultWrapper; public IResult<User> GetUser(int id) { if (id <= 0) return Result<User>.ValidationFail("Invalid user ID"); var user = _repository.FindById(id); if (user == null) return Result<User>.FailNotFound("User not found"); return Result<User>.Success(user, new MessageDetail("User retrieved successfully")); } // Usage var result = GetUser(123); if (result.Succeeded) { Console.WriteLine($"Found user: {result.Data.Name}"); } else { Console.WriteLine($"Error: {result.Message}"); } Features: Generic Result<T> and Result<T, E> for typed returns Factory methods: Success(), Fail(), ValidationFail(), FailNotFound() Structured messages with MessageDetail (code, severity, title, detail) Built-in logging integration with ILogger HTTP response conversion via ToResultAsync() 2. Timezone-Aware Date/Time Service Cross-platform timezone handling with dependency injection support. using NuvTools.Common.Dates; using NuvTools.Common.Dates.Enumerations; // Configure in DI container services.AddDateTimeService(TimeZoneRegion.Brasilia); // Use in your service public class OrderService { private readonly IDateTimeService _dateTime; public OrderService(IDateTimeService dateTime) { _dateTime = dateTime; } public void CreateOrder() { var orderTime = _dateTime.Now; // Local time in Brasilia var utcTime = _dateTime.UtcNow; // Always UTC } } // Extension methods for conversion var localTime = DateTime.UtcNow.ToTimeZone(TimeZoneRegion.Tokyo, UtcDirection.FromUtc); Features: 19 predefined timezone regions (Brasilia, UTC, Tokyo, NYC, London, etc.) Automatic Windows/IANA timezone ID mapping IDateTimeService abstraction for testability Custom UTC offset support 3. Enhanced Enum Support Extract rich metadata from enums using DisplayAttribute and DescriptionAttribute. using NuvTools.Common.Enums; using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations; public enum Status { [Display(Name = "Active", ShortName = "ACT", Description = "Currently active")] Active = 1, [Display(Name = "Inactive", ShortName = "INA", Description = "Not active")] Inactive = 2 } public enum Priority { Low = 1, Medium = 2, High = 3 } // Extract metadata var name = Status.Active.GetName(); // "Active" var shortName = Status.Active.GetShortName(); // "ACT" var description = Status.Active.GetDescription(); // "Currently active" // Convert to list for dropdowns var statusList = Enumeration.ToList<Status>(); // Find enum by metadata var status = Enumeration.GetEnumByShortName<Status>("ACT"); // Status.Active // Concatenate enum values into a composite integer int composite = Enumeration.ConcatEnumValues(Status.Active, Priority.High); // Result: 13 (concatenation of "1" + "3") int multiValue = Enumeration.ConcatEnumValues(Status.Active, Status.Inactive, Priority.Medium); // Result: 122 (concatenation of "1" + "2" + "2") Features: Extract Name, ShortName, Description, GroupName from DisplayAttribute Fallback to DescriptionAttribute when DisplayAttribute is not present Convert enums to lists for UI dropdowns with sorting options Find enum values by metadata (name, short name, description) Concatenate multiple enum values into a single composite integer Support for different underlying types (int, byte, short, long) 4. String Extensions Powerful string manipulation utilities. using NuvTools.Common.Strings; // Extract substrings string text = "Hello World"; text.Left(5); // "Hello" text.Right(5); // "World" // Remove diacritics "Olá, Mundo!".RemoveDiacritics(); // "Ola, Mundo!" // Advanced formatting with named placeholders var template = "Hello {name}, you have {count} messages"; template.Format(new Dictionary<string, object> { { "name", "John" }, { "count", 5 } }); // "Hello John, you have 5 messages" // Extract numbers "ABC-123-XYZ-456".GetNumbersOnly(); // "123456" // Validate JSON string json = "{\"key\":\"value\"}"; bool isValid = json.IsValidJson(); // true 5. Safe Number Parsing Parse strings to numeric types with null or zero fallback. using System.Globalization; using NuvTools.Common.Numbers; string value = "123"; long? number = value.ParseToLongOrNull(); // 123 string invalid = "abc"; long? nullResult = invalid.ParseToLongOrNull(); // null long zeroResult = invalid.ParseToLongOrNull(returnZeroIsNull: true); // 0 // Also available for int, short, decimal and double int? intValue = "42".ParseToIntOrNull(); // Without a provider the text is read in the current culture, which decides the decimal // separator: on a pt-BR machine "3.14" is 314. Text written by a machine — a file, a database // column, an API — has a fixed format, so pass the culture it was written in. decimal? area = "1521.202".ParseToDecimalOrNull(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // 1521.202 double? latitude = "-23.56287".ParseToDoubleOrNull(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // -23.56287 6. Web Utilities Generate and parse query strings from objects. using NuvTools.Common.Web; public class SearchRequest { public string Query { get; set; } public int Page { get; set; } public DateTime? StartDate { get; set; } } var request = new SearchRequest { Query = "test", Page = 1, StartDate = DateTime.Now }; // Convert to query string string url = request.GetQueryString("https://api.example.com/search"); // Result: https://api.example.com/search?Query=test&Page=1&StartDate=2025-12-06T10:30:00 // Parse query string back var dict = "?Query=test&Page=1".ParseQueryString(); 7. Exception Utilities Aggregate multi-level exception messages for better error reporting. using NuvTools.Common.Exceptions; try { // Code that throws nested exceptions } catch (Exception ex) { // Get all inner exception messages string fullMessage = ex.AggregateExceptionMessages(level: 3); // Result: "Level 0: Outer exception -> Level 1: Inner exception -> Level 2: Root cause" } 8. Stream Extensions Convert streams to byte arrays with sync and async support. using NuvTools.Common.IO; // Async byte[] bytes = await stream.ToByteListAsync(); // Sync byte[] bytes = stream.ToByteList(); 9. Assembly Reflection Extract metadata from assemblies. using NuvTools.Common.Reflection; var assembly = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly(); var info = assembly.ProgramInfo(); Console.WriteLine($"Name: {info.Name}"); Console.WriteLine($"Version: {info.Version}"); Console.WriteLine($"Description: {info.Description}"); // List all referenced assemblies var components = assembly.ListComponent(); 10. JSON Serialization Deep cloning and serialization utilities. using NuvTools.Common.Serialization.Json; var original = new MyObject { Name = "Test" }; var clone = original.Clone(); string json = original.Serialize(); var deserialized = json.Deserialize<MyObject>(); Why NuvTools.Common? ✅ Type-Safe - Strong typing and generics throughout ✅ Null-Safe - Nullable reference types enabled with defensive coding ✅ Async-First - Modern async/await patterns with ConfigureAwait(false) ✅ Minimal Dependencies - Only depends on Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions ✅ Cross-Platform - Works on Windows, Linux, and macOS ✅ Well-Documented - Complete XML documentation for IntelliSense ✅ Battle-Tested - Strong-named, production-ready code ✅ Multi-Targeted - Supports .NET 8, 9, and 10 Supported Frameworks .NET 8.0 .NET 9.0 .NET 10.0 Requirements No external dependencies (except Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions for logging integration) Works with Web, Desktop, Console, and MAUI applications Documentation All public APIs include comprehensive XML documentation. IntelliSense will show detailed information about: Method purposes and usage Parameter descriptions Return values Exception scenarios Code examples Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request. Releasing Publishing to nuget.org is irreversible per version, so the workflow makes it the last and smallest step. The package has its own workflow, and the steps live in the reusable package-publish.yml, the same layout as the other NuvTools repositories. Package Workflow Release tag NuvTools.Common common-publish.yml common-vX.Y.Z Set the package's <Version> in its .csproj and merge it. That is the version that gets published; the workflow reads it and never computes one. Run the library's workflow by hand (Actions → Common Publish → Run workflow) with push checked. The workflow builds the solution with -warnaserror, runs the tests, takes that package only from the build output, verifies it carries its README, licence, icon, symbols and every target framework, and then waits for approval on the nuget GitHub Environment before pushing. After the push succeeds, the workflow tags the commit with the tag in the table above. The tag is a record of what is on nuget.org, never what starts a release, so it cannot exist for a version that did not get there. A run whose tag already exists stops before building: the version has been released and <Version> needs a bump. Versions published by hand are refused. Releases made before these workflows exist on nuget.org with no tag. Pushing one again would skip the duplicate and then tag the current commit as a release it is not, so a version that is already on nuget.org stops the run. The exception is a re-run of the same run, which is how a push that succeeded and a tag that failed gets finished. No API key is stored. The push uses nuget.org's trusted publishing: the job presents a GitHub OIDC token, nuget.org checks it against the policy registered for this repository and answers with a key that lives for one hour. The repository needs one secret, NUGET_USER — the nuget.org profile name the policy belongs to — and the policy itself, registered under Trusted Publishing on nuget.org with the owner nuvtools, the repository nuvtools-common, the workflow file and the environment nuget. guides/foundation/validation/README.html.title: NuvTools Validation Library | Nuv Tools Framework
guides/foundation/validation/README.html.summary: NuvTools Validation Library A validation library for .NET applications, providing robust validation features for Web, Desktop, and Mobile (MAUI) applications. Includes email and numeric validators, specialized Brazilian document validators (CPF, CNPJ, phone, CEP), password complexity attributes, and data annotations. This library targets modern .NET platforms, including .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. Installation Install via NuGet Package Manager: dotnet add package NuvTools.Validation Or via Package Manager Console: Install-Package NuvTools.Validation Key Features General Validators: Email, numeric types (int, long, decimal), Base64/Data URI validation Brazilian Document Validators: CPF, CNPJ (including the new RFB alphanumeric format), mobile phone, and ZIP code (CEP) validation Document Formatting: CPF and CNPJ formatting helpers Data Annotations: CPF/CNPJ validation attributes, password complexity attributes Localized Messages: Validation messages in English and Portuguese (pt-BR) Quick Start General Validation using NuvTools.Validation; // Email validation bool isValid = "user@example.com".IsEmail(); // Numeric validation bool isInt = "12345".IsIntNumber(); bool isPositive = "12345".IsIntNumber(positiveOnly: true); bool isLong = "12345".IsLongNumber(); // Decimal validation bool isDecimal = "123.45".IsDecimalNumber(); Brazilian Document Validation using NuvTools.Validation.Brazil; // Validate CPF bool isValid = "123.456.789-01".IsCPF(); // Validate CNPJ (numeric) bool isValid = "12.345.678/0001-95".IsCNPJ(); // Validate CNPJ (new RFB alphanumeric format — uppercase A–Z and 0–9 in positions 1–12) bool isValidAlpha = "12.ABC.345/01DE-35".IsCNPJ(); // Auto-detect CPF or CNPJ bool isValid = "12345678901".IsCPForCNPJ(); // Validate mobile phone bool isValid = "11987654321".IsMobileNumber(); // Validate ZIP code (CEP) bool isValid = "01310-100".IsZipCodeNumber(); Document Formatting using NuvTools.Validation.Brazil; // Format CPF string formatted = "12345678901".FormatCPF(); // Output: 123.456.789-01 // Format CNPJ string formatted = "12345678000195".FormatCNPJ(); // Output: 12.345.678/0001-95 Data Annotations using NuvTools.Validation.Brazil.Annotations; using NuvTools.Validation.Annotations; public class UserRegistrationModel { [Required] [CPF] public string CPF { get; set; } [Required] [PasswordComplexityCapitalLetters(2)] [PasswordComplexityLowerCaseLetters(2)] [PasswordComplexityDigits(2)] public string Password { get; set; } } public class CompanyModel { [Required] [CNPJ] public string CNPJ { get; set; } } // Validate using data annotations var model = new UserRegistrationModel { CPF = "123.456.789-01", Password = "MyPass123" }; var errors = model.Validate(); // Returns null if valid, or list of error messages Features Multi-targeting: Compatible with .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10 Comprehensive documentation: Full XML documentation for IntelliSense Modern C# features: Uses nullable reference types, implicit usings, and source-generated regex Building from Source This project uses the modern .slnx solution format (Visual Studio 2022 v17.11+). # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/nuvtools/nuvtools-validation.git cd nuvtools-validation # Build the solution dotnet build NuvTools.Validation.slnx # Run tests dotnet test NuvTools.Validation.slnx # Create release packages dotnet build NuvTools.Validation.slnx --configuration Release Requirements .NET 8.0 SDK or higher Visual Studio 2022 (v17.11+) or Visual Studio Code with C# extension Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please feel free to submit a Pull Request. Releasing Publishing to nuget.org is irreversible per version, so the workflow makes it the last and smallest step. The package has its own workflow, and the steps live in the reusable package-publish.yml, the same layout as the other NuvTools repositories. Package Workflow Release tag NuvTools.Validation validation-publish.yml validation-vX.Y.Z Set the package's <Version> in its .csproj and merge it. That is the version that gets published; the workflow reads it and never computes one. Run the library's workflow by hand (Actions → Validation Publish → Run workflow) with push checked. The workflow builds the solution with -warnaserror, runs the tests, takes that package only from the build output, verifies it carries its README, licence, icon, symbols and every target framework, and then waits for approval on the nuget GitHub Environment before pushing. After the push succeeds, the workflow tags the commit with the tag in the table above. The tag is a record of what is on nuget.org, never what starts a release, so it cannot exist for a version that did not get there. A run whose tag already exists stops before building: the version has been released and <Version> needs a bump. Versions published by hand are refused. Releases made before these workflows exist on nuget.org with no tag. Pushing one again would skip the duplicate and then tag the current commit as a release it is not, so a version that is already on nuget.org stops the run. The exception is a re-run of the same run, which is how a push that succeeded and a tag that failed gets finished. No API key is stored. The push uses nuget.org's trusted publishing: the job presents a GitHub OIDC token, nuget.org checks it against the policy registered for this repository and answers with a key that lives for one hour. The repository needs one secret, NUGET_USER — the nuget.org profile name the policy belongs to — and the policy itself, registered under Trusted Publishing on nuget.org with the owner nuvtools, the repository nuvtools-validation, the workflow file and the environment nuget. Run a library's workflow by hand with push unchecked for a dry run that stops after the verification. License This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.
